Alcohol.note: Dosing based on standard drinks; effect varies with body water content.

Benzodiazepines.note: Doses typically in mg/kg for therapeutic use; recreational doses weight-sensitive.

Cannabis.note: THC effects largely independent of body weight; titration by inhalation.

Cocaine.note: Cardiovascular effects and toxicity correlate with body mass.

Ketamine.note: Clinical dosing in mg/kg; recreational users often dose by feel, but toxicity weight-related.

Kratom.note: Alkaloid effects scale with body weight; typical doses in grams.

LSD.note: Microgram doses; effects minimally influenced by body weight.

MDMA.note: Typical dose ~1.5 mg/kg; heavier individuals require more for same effect.

Nitrous_Oxide.note: Inhaled gas; effect depends on concentration and duration, not body weight.

Opioids_(Heroin/Fentanyl).note: Respiratory depression risk scales with mg/kg; fentanyl's narrow window highly weight-sensitive.

Psilocybin.note: Effects primarily set and setting; body weight minor factor.

Suboxone.note: Buprenorphine dosing in mg; sublingual absorption variable, but weight influences plasma levels.

Tramadol.note: Doses in mg; seizure risk and serotonin syndrome may be weight-related.

Alcohol.lethal_dose_reference: LD50 ~5-8 g/kg (350-560 g for 70 kg adult); acute poisoning >300 g

Benzodiazepines.lethal_dose_reference: LD50 unknown in humans; lethal solo rare, but >10 mg combined with depressants dangerous

Cannabis.lethal_dose_reference: No documented lethal overdose; estimated LD50 >> 1 g/kg THC

Cocaine.lethal_dose_reference: LD50 ~500 mg-1 g (variable by route); 1.2 g reported fatal

Ketamine.lethal_dose_reference: LD50 ~600 mg/kg in animals; human fatalities rare >500 mg with depressants

Kratom.lethal_dose_reference: No documented LD50; fatalities only with adulterants

LSD.lethal_dose_reference: LD50 ~100 mg/kg in animals; human LD50 > 10 mg

MDMA.lethal_dose_reference: LD50 ~ 10-20 mg/kg; fatalities > 200 mg with hyperthermia

Nitrous_Oxide.lethal_dose_reference: Hypoxia from oxygen displacement; no toxic LD50

Opioids_(Heroin/Fentanyl).lethal_dose_reference: Morphine LD50 ~200 mg; fentanyl LD50 ~2 mg for opioid-naive

Psilocybin.lethal_dose_reference: LD50 > 1 g/kg in animals; no human fatalities

Suboxone.lethal_dose_reference: Ceiling effect limits respiratory depression; deaths only with benzodiazepines/alcohol

Tramadol.lethal_dose_reference: LD50 ~ 500 mg/kg in animals; human fatalities > 1 g with seizures

Benzodiazepines.mechanism: Synergistic CNS depression leading to respiratory failure and coma.
Benzodiazepines.notes: Both potentiate GABA; benzodiazepine clearance may be reduced by alcohol.

Cannabis.mechanism: Additive cognitive and motor impairment, increased accident risk.
Cannabis.citation: TripSit Combination Chart 2024; Sewell et al. 2009
Cannabis.notes: THC may increase alcohol absorption; both impair driving.

Cocaine.mechanism: Formation of cocaethylene, increasing cardiotoxicity and risk of sudden death.
Cocaine.citation: Drugs.com Interaction Checker; Pennings et al. 2002
Cocaine.notes: Cocaethylene has longer half-life; increases myocardial oxygen demand.

Ketamine.notes: Ketamine's dissociative effects mask intoxication, leading to overconsumption.

Kratom.mechanism: Additive sedative effects, especially at high kratom doses.
Kratom.citation: TripSit; CDC SUDORS (kratom co-detected with alcohol)
Kratom.notes: Kratom's opioid-like effects at high doses compound alcohol sedation.

LSD.mechanism: No significant physical interaction; alcohol may dull the psychedelic experience.
LSD.notes: Psychological effects may be altered, but no physical synergy.

MDMA.mechanism: Increased risk of dehydration, hyperthermia, and neurotoxicity.
MDMA.notes: Alcohol exacerbates MDMA-induced dehydration and hyperthermia.

Nitrous_Oxide.mechanism: Additive CNS depression, increased risk of falls and hypoxia.
Nitrous_Oxide.notes: Nitrous displaces oxygen; alcohol impairs compensatory responses.

Opioids_(Heroin/Fentanyl).mechanism: Synergistic respiratory depression, leading to fatal overdose.
Opioids_(Heroin/Fentanyl).notes: Even small amounts of alcohol can precipitate fatal respiratory arrest with opioids.

Psilocybin.mechanism: Minimal physical interaction; may alter subjective effects.
Psilocybin.notes: No known physical interaction; psychological effects may be intensified.

Suboxone.mechanism: Additive respiratory depression despite buprenorphine's ceiling effect.
Suboxone.notes: Alcohol can overcome buprenorphine's ceiling; benzodiazepines often co-involved.

Tramadol.mechanism: Additive CNS depression and lowered seizure threshold.
Tramadol.notes: Tramadol's SNRI effects may increase seizure risk; alcohol lowers threshold further.

Cannabis.mechanism: Mild additive sedation, not clinically dangerous.
Cannabis.notes: THC may increase anxiety in some, but no dangerous synergy.

Cocaine.mechanism: Cocaine's stimulant effects may mask benzodiazepine sedation, increasing cardiovascular strain.
Cocaine.notes: Benzodiazepines are sometimes used to comedown from cocaine, but timing matters.

Ketamine.notes: Both potentiate GABA and NMDA antagonism; profound sedation.

Kratom.notes: Kratom's mu-opioid activity at high doses adds sedation.

LSD.mechanism: Benzodiazepines are used to abort bad trips; no adverse synergy.

MDMA.mechanism: Benzodiazepines may blunt MDMA's effects and increase sedation.

Opioids_(Heroin/Fentanyl).mechanism: Synergistic respiratory depression, leading to fatal overdose.

Cocaine.mechanism: Increased heart rate and anxiety, possible panic attacks.
